NEW DELHI: The Ladakh outfits in talks with the home ministry on safeguards for the Union territory, have been asked to come up with a draft proposal addressing seven key questions relating to the larger governance structure for Ladakh, including the division of powers and functions between the proposed UT-level body and the seven district councils.Sources involved in the ongoing dialogue process between the home ministry and Ladakh administration on one side and the Leh Apex Body (LAB), Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and activist Sonam Wangchuk, on the other, told TOI that the latest round on Sept 9 saw a presentation being made by the MHA on different aspects of the proposed governance structure involving the three tiers, the apex UT-level body, autonomous district councils and the panchayats.The first question sought suggestions on the name of the UT-level legislative body as well as its executive arm. A key angle discussed was the proposed representation of LAHDC representatives in the UT-level body. The Ladakh representatives were asked if they favour direct elections to the UT-level legislative body, with the members representing different constituencies to be carved through delimitation. The LAHDC would thus have no direct representation in the UT-level body.Alternatively, it was proposed that the UT-level body may be indirectly elected by the LAHDCs. A consensus emerged in favour of direct elections.As for the district councils, they will also have direct elections, as per the process already followed for the existing two councils in Ladakh and Kargil.The third question focused on functions that should necessarily be exercised by the UT-level body “in the interest of uniformity, coordinated development and effective administration”. The MHA officials assured that the UT-level body would be given charge of matters related to land, culture and heritage, environment, mineral resources as well as those covered under Article 240 of the Constitution of India.The Ladakh representatives were asked what functions should remain at the district level, so as to protect local interests and ensure responsive governance. Also, they were asked to specify what principles should guide the allocation of powers between the UT-level body and LAHDCs; the options being local preference, administrative efficiency and uniformity of policy.Another poser to LAB, KDA and Wangchuk related to subjects that should fall within the law-making domain of the UT-level elected body, which shall be in tune with the basis structure of the Constitution.The Ladakh bodies were told to submit their answers to the seven queries so that a draft proposal could be prepared for the next round of discussions likely in October. Since the proposed governance structure is expected to be a unique model, legal opinion will have to be taken before finalising the legislative framework.Notwithstanding the progress made in the Sept 9 discussions, LAB, KDA and Wangchuk had expressed disappointment with the lack of “headway” in the discussions, a day later. When contacted, Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra disagreed and insisted that the talks were productive, with the entire legislative process of creation of the UT-level body as well as autonomous councils in the five new Ladakh districts, explained in detail to the Ladakh representatives. They were told that a Constitutional amendment would have to be passed by Parliament along with a separate legislation detailing the powers and responsibilities of different tiers of the proposed governance structure.“Clarity was offered on the proposed constitutional safeguards. Besides, an assurance was given to the Ladakh bodies that their demand for withdrawal of cases related to the violent events of September 24, 2025 as well as compensation would be put up before the Ladakh LG,” said Kundra.The LG, in fact, accepted the demand on Sunday, announcing a compensation of Rs 15 lakh each to the next kin of those killed, Rs 3 lakh for those who sustained minor injuries and Rs 1 lakh for ones with minor injuries.While all other Ladakh representatives sounded positive at the end of the Sept 9 talks, Wangchuk is said to have demanded that no major decisions regarding the proposed powers of the UT-level body be taken till it is in place.This demand was however rejected by MHA which reminded him that the Ladakh LG was empowered by the Constitution to take decisions related to administration and governance, and that there could not be a void.Sources in Ladakh govt indicated that not all Ladakh representatives may be on the same page on the call to revive the agitation in view of the “failure” of Sept 9 talks. “The prime mover of the agitation plan is Wangchuk; the others are not in favour of a belligerent approach and prefer to build on the progress achieved in the talks so far,” said an officer.
Article Summary: Ladakh outfits in talks with the home ministry on safeguards for the Union territory. They have been asked to come up with a draft proposal addressing seven key questions relating to the larger governance structure for Ladakh. These include the division of powers and functions between the proposed UT-level body and the seven district councils.

Article Title: Ladakh begins reviving Tso Kar glacial lake
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: To revive the rapidly shrinking Tso Kar glacial lake, Ladakh administration has launched a project to divert an average of 132 cusecs (around 320 million litres) of untapped glacier water daily from Rupsho Kharnak stream in Changthang district to the lake. Officials expect the lake will be restored to its former glory within a year, calling it the first project of its scale in India to revive a high-altitude lake under such harsh climatic conditions.Situated at an altitude of nearly 15,000ft, the lake has lost nearly 70% of its water over the past decade, shrinking from around 11,000 acres to just 3,200 acres. Once a thriving habitat for migratory birds, including the black-necked crane, it now attracts far fewer birds.The project follows the successful diversion of 90 million litres of Stok glacier water into irrigation canals in Igoo-Phey and Chuchot villages near Leh. The administration described it as the region’s second major water-management initiative of its kind.The revival was conceived after Lt Governor VK Saxena visited Tso Kar on Aug 10. Villagers told him the lake once supported centuries-old salt trade and maintained a delicate ecological balance, but its decline had resulted in loss of grazing land and shrinking bird populations.Saxena directed the public health engineering department to survey the area. Its report, submitted on Aug 30 after 15 days of groundwork, proposed an 11km RCC channel. Saxena, however, ruled out a new RCC structure and suggested first diverting the water to a depression through a simple earthen channel. Work began on Sept 2, ahead of the winter freeze.Rupsho Kharnak stream, located about 11km from Tso Kar at an altitude of 18,000ft, has a peak summer discharge of around 132 cusecs. So far, 20 cusecs is being diverted to the first depression, which has filled by about 20% in four days using an earthen channel and a defunct concrete canal built in 1995.Before reaching Tso Kar, water will fill three natural depressions, creating freshwater wetlands of 270, 24 and 10 acres with a combined capacity of nearly 1,230 million litres. The wetlands will allow sediments to settle, ensuring cleaner water reaches the lake, while also creating new habitats for migratory birds and potential tourist attractions visible from Leh-Manali highway.
Article Summary: Tso Kar glacial lake has lost nearly 70% of its water over the past decade. Officials expect the lake will be restored to its former glory within a year. The project follows the successful diversion of 90 million litres of Stok glacier water into irrigation canals near Leh.

Appreciating her thought, Dhami said it reflected a positive mindset.He said circumstances could be challenging, but the resolve to achieve something better in life should remain strong. He urged the youth of Uttarakhand to move forward with the aim of turning challenges into opportunities.Student Srishti raised questions about people's trust in government schools and hospitals. Responding to her, the Chief Minister said personalities such as APJ Abdul Kalam and Prime Minister Narendra Modi had risen from ordinary families to occupy the highest positions in the country.He said young people had an important role to play in improving systems. The present generation, he said, understood what was good and better, and students should remain aware of development works and various systems in their districts and the state and contribute towards bringing about positive change, the release said.Anushka, a student from Rudraprayag, shared her views on preventing migration. Dhami said the geographical conditions of Uttarakhand were challenging, but the government was working to provide electricity, water and other basic facilities in villages across the state.He said much more remained to be done, and the government was continuously working in this direction. The Chief Minister said more than 500 smart classes were currently operational in the state and reverse migration was also taking place.As per the release, the Chief Minister urged the youth not to remain merely job seekers but to aim at becoming job creators.Ishika Negi and Gaurav Bisht shared suggestions related to tourism, environmental conservation and the Char Dham pilgrimage. Students also expressed their views on protecting Uttarakhand's natural resources while linking tourism with employment generation and the local economy.Student Mukesh Kushwaha suggested extending facilities such as helicopter ambulances to small villages to improve healthcare access and providing skill-development training at the school level.Calling the suggestion important, Dhami said the government's endeavour was to provide young people with the necessary facilities and opportunities to make the best use of their talent and capabilities. He said continuous efforts were being made to make youth self-reliant through skill development and employment-oriented education.The Chief Minister said all the ideas and suggestions put forward by the students should be taken seriously. He said every individual had an important role in building a developed India and a developed Uttarakhand.He also urged the youth to stay away from drugs and channelise their energy in a positive direction while ensuring their active participation in nation-building.Dhami said the day was special for him as he had the opportunity to interact directly with students. Their views, he said, reflected their vision, knowledge, sensitivity and thoughts about the future, the release said.He said all the students demonstrated a strong desire to move forward and achieve something better. This energy, he said, was the greatest strength in building a developed Uttarakhand.The Chief Minister said the youth were the future of the country and that the Uttarakhand and India of tomorrow would be shaped by their dreams, resolve and hard work.He said it was important to understand what India should look like in 2047, what contribution the youth should make, what role they should play and how systems should function. The participation and vision of young people on these issues, he said, were extremely important.Dhami said every young person had a significant role in the development journey and urged them to turn their dreams into goals and continue moving forward with determination.The Chief Minister said young people from Uttarakhand were performing well in various fields. He said initiatives such as the Mukhyamantri Yuva Yojana were being undertaken to promote the talent of youth in technology and innovation, the release said.He also said the state government had enacted strict laws against those involved in examination malpractice and cheating, ensuring that meritorious youth received transparent and fair opportunities.During the programme, student Aditi Gautam presented a painting made by her to Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami.Teacher and nodal officer Ankush was honoured for ensuring better participation in the programme. Rudraprayag District Magistrate Vishal Mishra was also honoured for ensuring 100 per cent participation of students from the district in the essay competition.The Chief Minister extended his best wishes to the students and urged them to make their dreams their goals, work hard consistently and utilise their talent and energy in the development of the state and the country, the release said.He said the Uttarakhand of the future would be the Uttarakhand of the dreams of its youth, and every young person in the state would have an important role in building it.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday participated in the 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan' programme. The programme was organised on the theme 'Mere Sapno Ka Uttarakhand' He held a direct interaction with students from across the state and sought to understand their views, suggestions and aspirations.

Article Title: Mamata's TMC faction names candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls in Bengal
Article Text:
TMC names Sanchita Pradhan, Rabiul Alam Chowdhury candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls

NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction led by Mamata Banerjee on Sunday announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury as its candidates for the October 6 bypolls to the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats, respectively. The counting of votes is set to take place on October 9.Pradhan is a new face, while Chowdhury is a former MLA, news agency PTI reports.The announcement comes after an earlier rebel TMC faction said it would support Mamata Banerjee, strengthening the party's position ahead of the bypolls.The Nandigram bypoll was necessitated after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the seat and chose to retain Bhabanipur, where he defeated TMC chief Mamata Banerjee in the Assembly elections held earlier this year. The Rejinagar seat fell vacant after Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) founder Humayun Kabir resigned from the seat, having also won from Nowda.The two seats are expected to witness a keen political contest, with the bypoll results likely to be closely watched ahead of the next electoral battle in the state.
Article Summary: TMC names Sanchita Pradhan, Rabiul Alam Chowdhury candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls. The counting of votes is set to take place on October 9. The announcement comes after an earlier rebel TMC faction said it would support Mamata Banerjee.

Article Title: 'Not our culture to impose Emergency, we believe in dialogue': Amit Shah on Gen-Z led movements
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government believes in dialogue and discussion while addressing questions on the social and political impact of various Gen Z-led movements.Shah said at a press conference that people in a democracy have the right to express their views, asserting that a BJP-led government cannot impose an Emergency."We are in a democracy. People hold different views on various issues, and it is essential that those views are expressed. The Bharatiya Janata Party is in power, but we cannot govern by imposing an Emergency. That is the Congress culture, not ours. We believe in dialogue and discussion," Shah said.Asked whether the National Register of Citizens (NRC) would be implemented in Manipur using the 1951 baseline before the elections, and whether there was a deadline for its nationwide implementation, Shah said the government was discussing the issues with its colleagues and political parties in Manipur."We are discussing both these matters with our colleagues as well as with the political parties in Manipur. As soon as any decision is taken, we will inform you," he said.On tensions over language and regional identity linked to migration, Shah said the government’s policy was to give priority to the mother tongue, adding that the Constitution had laid down specific directives for states on the issue.\"It is our government's policy to prioritise the mother tongue, and the Constitution has also issued specific directives to the states in this regard. I do not believe this will become a major issue. While isolated incidents may occur if certain individuals attempt to stoke tensions, the states have experienced leadership and will certainly find a way to resolve such issues," Shah added.He also added that PM Modi was the first prime minister in six decades, since the early years after Independence, to be elected to office three times, calling it a reflection of his 25-year political record.Shah said the country had pursued a strong foreign and defence policy based on the principle of “India First”, while the economy had risen from being counted among the ‘Fragile Five’ to the world’s top five. He also cited 7.8 per cent GDP growth in the first quarter as evidence of India’s strong economic performance.Shah was addressing a press conference to announce the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan”, scheduled from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday and his 25 years in public life in Gujarat and at the Centre.Shah said the BJP, its allies and people across the country would jointly organise the month-long campaign from September 17, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.He said the BJP had earlier observed Modi’s birthday as ‘Seva Saptah’ from September 17 to October 2, while some places extended the celebrations for a week. However, this year’s celebrations would be special as Modi will complete 25 years in public office as chief minister and prime minister on October 7.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government believes in dialogue and discussion. Shah was addressing a press conference to announce the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’, scheduled from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.

Article Title: 'Unacceptable': India condemns attack on commercial vessel off Oman, 13 Indians rescued
Article Text:
India condemns attack, 13 of 14 Indian crew rescued from vessel off Oman (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Sunday condemned an attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman, saying 13 of the 14 Indian crew members onboard had been rescued while search and rescue operations continued for the missing Indian national.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said the Indian Embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with Omani authorities. The statement came as an Iranian cargo vessel was also reported to have been struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting one death and four injuries.“We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman earlier today. Of the 14 Indian crew onboard, 13 Indians have been rescued so far. Search and Rescue operations for the missing Indian national are continuing,” the MEA said.The ministry said it had reiterated India's call for immediate de-escalation and the use of dialogue and diplomacy to restore peace in the region.The MEA said the targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians and civilian infrastructure in the region was unacceptable.“We reiterate our call for immediate de-escalation of tensions and pursuance of dialogue and diplomacy to bring peace to the region. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in the region is unacceptable,” it said.India also called for the restoration of safe navigation and commercial traffic through international waterways in the region.“We also urge that free and safe navigation and flow of commerce through the international waterways in the region be restored at the earliest,” the MEA said.The Indian statement came amid renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, where an Iranian cargo vessel was reportedly struck early Sunday near Qeshm Island.Iranian state media said the attack killed one person and wounded four others. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations monitor separately said a vessel had been hit by a projectile while transiting the strait, triggering a fire and an evacuation operation, although it was not immediately clear whether it was the same incident.Iran's state-run IRNA quoted the governor of Qeshm as blaming a “terrorist enemy” for the attack.Hours before the reported strike, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said: “Our people can’t be bullied into submission. Iran won’t surrender,” according to a social media post.The attacks came a day before a planned meeting of foreign ministers from regional countries in Oman to discuss efforts by Iran and Oman to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Iran has said that an agreement with Oman on managing the waterway would not automatically mean that the strait would be reopened to shipping. Pezeshkian told India Today TV on Saturday: “The waterway would be opened up on the condition that the U.S. will terminate its blockade.”
Article Summary: India condemns attack, 13 of 14 Indian crew rescued from vessel off Oman. Search and rescue operations continue for missing Indian national. Iranian cargo vessel was also reported to have been struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting one death.

Article Title: 'Not IPL commentary': Congress takes shot at Ravi Shastri for post praising PM Modi
Article Text:
Congress reacts to Ravi Shastri post

NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday hit out at Indian cricket commentator Ravi Shastri after he praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s interaction with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Brics 2026 Summit.Shastri on X wrote, “Never felt prouder as an Indian. President Putin. President Xi. And our Magnificent Prime Minister Narendra Modi together in Mother India. International diplomacy like never before. Take a Bow. Modi Ji.”Reacting to the post, Congress leader Pawan Khera said it was “too much to expect” Shastri to remember a similar diplomatic moment involving former PM Manmohan Singh in New Delhi in 2012.Congress said Singh was flanked by then Chinese president Hu Jintao and Russian president Dmitry Medvedev in New Delhi on March 29, 2012.Taking a dig at Shastri’s cricketing background, Indian Youth Congress former president Srinivas BV added, “Ravi bhai, this isn’t IPL commentary. You can’t call every familiar shot ‘never seen before.’ India was playing international diplomacy long before your current sponsor arrived.”The party further alleged that the posts praising the Modi government were being dictated by the Prime Minister’s Office.“Btw, we know who in the PMO is dictating these promotional posts!” Congress said.
Article Summary: Ravi Shastri praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's interaction with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Brics 2026 Summit. Congress leader Pawan Khera said it was “too much to expect’ Shstri to remember a similar diplomatic moment involving former PM Manmohan Singh in New Delhi in 2012.

Article Title: ‘We will continue in Congress’: Konda Surekha rules out joining another party, eyes 2028 polls
Article Text:
File photo: Former Telangana minister Konda Surekha (Picture credit: ANI)

Surekha says Congress leadership is in touch

Removed from cabinet after controversy

Other changes in Telangana Congress

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Telangana minister Konda Surekha , who was recently dropped from chief minister A Revanth Reddy’s Cabinet, on Sunday said she would remain with the Congress and contest the next Assembly elections in 2028.Addressing a meeting of her supporters in Warangal, Surekha said she and her husband Konda Murali would continue working for the people irrespective of whether she held any official position.“We are told not to go anywhere (join any other party) and that the party will take care of us. We are telling them that we have no intention to join any other party. We will continue in Congress. We will definitely contest on behalf of Congress. We will win and ensure Congress returns to power,” she said.Surekha also expressed confidence that she would receive the Congress ticket to contest from the Warangal East constituency in the 2028 Assembly polls. She said she would be re-elected as an MLA and become a minister again.Her remarks came amid reports that the Congress leadership has been reaching out to her following her removal from the state Cabinet.Surekha said she had been receiving calls and was being told not to join any other party.She reiterated that she had no intention of leaving the Congress.She said she and Murali would continue to work on people's issues and ensure development in the constituency even without holding government posts.Surekha was dropped from the Cabinet on September 3 following a controversy over remarks made against Revanth Reddy and others by her daughter, Konda Sushmitha Patel.Surekha had subsequently accused the chief minister of resorting to “blackmail politics” to secure her removal, claiming that the party high command was not in favour of the move.In earlier remarks, Surekha had questioned the decision to remove her, saying she had neither committed corruption nor been given an opportunity to explain herself.She had also defended her daughter, arguing that her comments were personal and should not be attributed to her.Surekha had questioned why she should be held responsible for remarks made by her adult daughter and referred to controversial statements made by other Congress leaders while questioning the action against her.She had also challenged the party leadership to take action against her and met Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in Delhi as the high command considered disciplinary action.The disciplinary action against Surekha was also accompanied by the removal of veteran Congress leader G Chinna Reddy as vice-chairman of the Telangana Planning Board.His removal followed a disciplinary committee recommendation over his remarks against Wanaparthy MLA T Megha Reddy.Meanwhile, Revanth Reddy announced three appointments: Gadwal Vijayalakshmi as vice-chairperson of the Telangana Planning Board, Nerella Sharada as chairperson of the Telangana State Commission for Women and former Rajya Sabha MP G Sudha Rani as chairperson of the Kakatiya Urban Development Authority.
Article Summary: Former Telangana minister Konda Surekha says she will remain with the Congress. She was recently dropped from chief minister A Revanth Reddy’s Cabinet.Surekha was dropped from the Cabinet on September 3 following a controversy over remarks made by her daughter.
